children: Google (GOOG) is planning an orbital test of its in-house AI computing hardware, marking an early engineering effort that could support future data-processing systems beyond Earth.

The test is part of Project Suncatcher and is slated to fly aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission with Planet. Google will examine whether its Tensor Processing Units, or TPUs, can handle launch conditions and operate amid radiation and temperature swings in low Earth orbit.

Prior testing of the company's Trillium TPUs found the chips could withstand radiation levels above those anticipated over a five-year mission. Google has also subjected the hardware to simulated launch shaking to study its durability.

Managing heat remains a technical challenge because standard air-based cooling does not work in a vacuum. Google is therefore studying heat pipes and radiators for thermal control, while longer-term plans include several satellites linked by lasers.
A two-satellite communications trial is targeted for 2027, with the initial mission focused on gathering engineering results rather than proving a commercial service.

title: Google AI Chips Blast Off -- SpaceX Mission Set to Test Orbital Computing
